sentences.ko: 아니, 내가 보기엔 누가 잘못했는지 뻔한데.
sentences.text: No, I think it's very obvious who's wrong here.

alts.text: Come on, it's pretty clear who messed up.
In my opinion, it is quite clear who is at fault in this situation.

sentences.note: 다툼에서 편을 들거나 내 생각을 분명히 할 때 **who's wrong here** 라고 해요. 앞에 **I think** 를 붙이면 말이 덜 세게 들려요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.text: Oh, I get to be in charge of cups and ice.

alts.text: Ooh, cups and ice are on me.
It appears that I will be responsible for the cups and the ice.

sentences.note: 파티 준비하면서 일을 나눌 때 **in charge of** 로 '~ 담당' 을 말해요. **I get to** 는 '~하게 됐네' 라는 뜻인데, 이렇게 시시한 일을 맡았을 때 살짝 비꼬는 말로도 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그리고… 내가 걔네한테 말했을 수도 있어.
sentences.text: And there's a slight chance I may have told them.

alts.text: Okay, so I might've kinda told them.
It is possible that I may have mentioned it to them.

sentences.note: 비밀을 흘린 걸 털어놓을 때 **there's a slight chance** 와 **may have told** 로 돌려 말해요. 실은 확실히 말했다는 게 다 보여서 우스운 말이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아무튼, 걔네가 토요일 밤에 우리 데리고 나가서 한턱내고 싶대.
sentences.text: Anyway, they want to take us out Saturday night.

alts.text: So they wanna take us out Saturday.
In any case, they would like to take us out on Saturday evening.

sentences.note: **take us out** 은 '우리를 데리고 나가서 밥이나 술을 사 준다' 는 뜻이에요. 딴 얘기를 하다 본론으로 돌아올 때 **Anyway** 로 시작해요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 지금 여동생이 전화 기다리고 있거든. 주말에 자기 별장 써도 된대, 가서 스키 타래.
sentences.text: Because I have my sister on hold and she said that we could have her cabin for the weekend and go skiing.

alts.text: My sister's waiting on the other line — we can use her cabin this weekend and hit the slopes.
My sister is waiting on the other line, and she has offered us her cabin for the weekend so that we can go skiing.

sentences.note: 통화하다가 상대를 잠깐 기다리게 해 둔 상태를 **on hold** 라고 해요. 남의 집을 빌려 쓸 때 **have her cabin** 처럼 have 만으로 '써도 된다' 를 말할 수 있어요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.text: Both logic and math are taking a serious hit today.

alts.text: Man, logic and math are getting wrecked today.
Today, logic and mathematics are suffering a serious blow.

sentences.note: **taking a serious hit** 는 '크게 타격을 입다'라는 뜻으로, 누가 말도 안 되는 소리를 할 때 농담 삼아 비꼬는 자리에서 씁니다. 돈·평판·자존심이 깎일 때도 그대로 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아니, 그냥… 사실 나도 그 사람이랑 사귀어 보고 싶었거든.
sentences.text: No, it's just cuz uh I I kind of wanted to go out with her too.

alts.text: Honestly, I kinda wanted to ask her out too.
The truth is that I also wanted to go out with her.

sentences.note: **go out with** 는 '~와 데이트하다, 사귀다'라는 뜻으로 연애 얘기에서 가장 흔히 씁니다. **kind of** 를 앞에 붙이면 속마음을 털어놓을 때 쑥스러움이 묻어납니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 응, 걔 안데스 산맥에서 넉 달 동안 트레킹하다가 막 돌아왔어.
sentences.text: Yeah, he just got back from like this four month trek in the Andes.

alts.text: Yep, he's just back from four months hiking the Andes.
He has just returned from a four-month trek in the Andes.

sentences.note: **just got back from** 은 '~에서 막 돌아왔다'로, 여행이나 출장에서 돌아온 사람 얘기를 전할 때 씁니다. **like this** 는 무언가를 처음 소개하며 말할 때 끼워 넣는 말버릇입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 너 걔랑은 거리 두는 게 좋겠어.
sentences.text: I think you should stay away from him.

alts.text: Steer clear of him, okay?
In my opinion, you should keep your distance from him.

sentences.note: **stay away from** 은 '~를 멀리하다'로, 친구에게 위험하거나 질 나쁜 사람을 조심하라고 충고할 때 씁니다. 더 편하게는 **Steer clear of** 라고 합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아 근데, 걔가 내 돈 몇 달러 슬쩍 가져갔어.
sentences.text: Hey, so he stole a couple bucks from me.

alts.text: Dude, he swiped a few bucks from me.
Actually, he stole a few dollars from me.

sentences.note: **a couple bucks** 는 '몇 달러'로, 큰돈이 아닌 소액을 말할 때 씁니다. bucks 는 dollars 의 구어이고, **swiped** 는 '슬쩍했다'는 가벼운 말입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends
